amended_entry: Section 6.1 per-subgroup stratified W2 recompute + per-family FDR (T1.28)
amendment_reason: Pre-dispatch verification (vault Computational-Log + on-disk artifacts) found the 2026-06-13 entry internally inconsistent: it adopts a per-subgroup-vs-own-Markov-1-null test model (forced by B2.6, whose mean-vs-mean T_ratio = Wbar(obs-null)/Wbar(null-null) is an observed-vs-own-null statistic and is incompatible with a pairwise A-vs-B comparison) but carries the legacy PAIRWISE test count '50 = 2+6+42'. Those are pairwise-between-subgroup counts over 2/3/7 subgroups (counted per H0/H1): gender C(2,2)*2=2, NS-SEC C(3,2)*2=6, cohort C(7,2)*2=42, confirmed against results/trajectory_tda_integration/06_stratified.json. Under the per-subgroup model the count is the number of SUBGROUPS, not pairs.

corrections.rationale: Per-subgroup model => one test per subgroup; 2/6/42 were pairwise counts.

corrections.to: NS-SEC = 3-class parental_nssec {Intermediate, Professional/Managerial, Routine/Manual}; cohort = 7 decade bins {1930s..1990s}
corrections.rationale: The '6' and '42' were pairwise-comparison counts of the 3- and 7-group axes, not subgroup counts; legacy 06_stratified.json group_sizes confirm 2/3/7.

BY's positive-dependence justification applied to adjacent-cohort PAIRWISE tests that shared panel observations. Per-subgroup-vs-own-null tests run on DISJOINT cohort subgroups => mutually independent => standard BH. Gender and NS-SEC families were already BH.

corrections.to: results/trajectory_tda_integration/embeddings.npy (27,280, USoc) and results/trajectory_tda_bhps/embeddings.npy (8,509, BHPS); subgroups are row-subsets of these locked embeddings
corrections.rationale: The Computational-Log fixes the canonical P01 / section-6.1 substrate as the 27,280 integration embedding (locked PCA-20/GMM row order). The 32,763-row results/trajectory_tda_full bundle (tfidf=true, evr 0.89, the only persisted scaler/pca joblib) is a DIFFERENT pipeline and is NOT the section-6.1 substrate. The frozen full-sample loadings are already baked into the locked embeddings, so subgroup analysis is a row-subset; no separate joblib transform is required.

corrections.to: per-individual gender / parental_nssec (3-class) / birth-decade cohort from the regression analytical frame (T1.20 assembly), ID-joined to the 27,280 (USoc) and 8,509 (BHPS) embedding rows; strata keys confirmed against legacy 06_stratified.json at assembly
corrections.rationale: Membership is absent from the trajectory outputs (05_analysis.json has only regimes/cycles/gmm_labels); it lives in the regression covariate assembly and must be row-joined to the embeddings.

unchanged.test_model: one Markov-1 W2 test PER SUBGROUP (subgroup observed PD vs its own frozen Markov-1 null)
unchanged.statistic: mean-vs-mean T_ratio = mean(W_obs-null) / mean(W_null-null), with 95% BCa CI (B2 / B2.6)
unchanged.complement: persistence-landscape L2 reported alongside W2 (mandatory dual-metric rule)

key_params.landmark_note: actual_landmarks = min(5000, subgroup_n); varying landmark fraction disclosed per the T1.26b lesson
key_params.effect_sizes: T_ratio + 95% BCa CI beside every raw and adjusted p

unchanged.reporting_protocol: report each subgroup's raw p, family-adjusted p, and effect size; flag significance per family. NOT an A/B/C prose-direction lock. Contingency: if a v1 section-6.1 subgroup heterogeneity claim CHANGES significance after recompute+FDR, surface to the User before section-6.1 v2 prose.

scientific_note: The per-subgroup model answers 'does each subgroup's topology exceed its own Markov-1 baseline?'. This is NOT the v1 section-6.1 pairwise heterogeneity question ('do subgroups differ from each other?'). The shift is a deliberate consequence of adopting the B2.6 mean-vs-mean obs-vs-null construction uniformly; section-6.1 v2 prose must frame the result as per-subgroup Markov-1 irreducibility, not between-subgroup difference. User-approved 2026-06-27.
